name: commons-colour-match-v1
description: ⭐ THE SECOND FALLBACK KNOB OF THE COMMONS, TURNED ON (C10, Dean 09/09/2026). rules.economy.commonsColourMatch true: the card you play onto a central board must MATCH that board's suit, with two cards of any suits standing in for one of the board's colour - the island's wild substitution rate, reused rather than re-rated (D5). The shipped rule is false: any card pays for any board, which is the sentence that makes the whole bonus one line of teach. ⭐ IT RATIONS A DIFFERENT THING FROM commons-threshold-2, WHICH IS WHY THERE ARE TWO KNOBS AND NOT ONE LADDER. A threshold rations HOW OFTEN the centre can be used; colour matching rations WHICH BOARD a given hand can afford. So this is the arm to run when the bonus RATE is inside Dean's 30-60% band but the DOOR MIX is not - and the door mix is the reading this project has moved most often and cares about most, because it is the one number that says whether all five actions are alive. Today a hand of Wheat buys any board, so the mix is a taste of the bots' evaluator rather than a constraint of the rules; under this arm it becomes a constraint. ⚠️ AND IT PUSHES HARD ON THE MONOCULTURE FINDING (v31 risk 3, and the Innovation lens's standing objection that the metric axis must not be the specialisation axis). Under matching, an own-suit hand can only ever afford its own board, so a seat farming Wheat buys Harvests all game. The own-crop build share was 82.6% before v31 and 83.3% after and has never been read under any later pass; it is the FIRST thing to re-read here, ahead of the door mix, because a door mix that looks more even across the TABLE can be five seats each locked to their own board, which is the opposite of what an even mix is supposed to mean. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) own-crop build share and the fee-suit mix together - are players paying junk, or paying the only thing that fits; (2) the door mix, and cross it with who bought what; (3) the bonus rate against the band, which should FALL, because a hand that cannot match cannot play; (4) the wild-pair share of all plays, which is the pressure gauge - under about a fifth and the colour keying is doing work, over about half and the matching rule is a tax that everybody is paying around. ⛔ TEACH COST IS A REAL PART OF THE VERDICT HERE, not a footnote: 'play any card' is one clause and 'play a matching card, or two of any' is three. The five-minute teach is a hard target, so this arm has to buy something visible to be worth adopting.
